subject: Geofence & retention: request for deletion evidence and certification
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <security@greenlinehealth.com>

Cc: compliance@greenlinehealth.com <compliance@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geofence & retention: evidence request for EU-only tenancy

Hi Marcus / Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward final procurement for our Private (VPC) deployment, our security/compliance team needs concrete evidence about how Redwood enforces EU-only residency and how deletion/retention is implemented end-to-end. In particular we need answers for:

- Scope: which artifacts are considered "customer data" (objects, DB snapshots, embeddings, logs, metrics) and their storage locations.
- Backups/snapshots: where are snapshots stored, is cross-region replication enabled by default, and what controls prevent unintended replication?
- Deletion workflow: steps when we request tenant deletion — what is deleted, what is retained (if anything), and how is deletion validated?
- KMS/key lifecycle: circumstances and process for rotating or destroying keys that encrypted our data.
- Evidence: sample deletion certificate or manifest we can accept as proof for auditors.

I attached a short questionnaire (initial-compliance-questions.xlsx). Can you confirm what evidence you can provide and an approximate SLA for producing it (we're targeting a procurement milestone next week)?

Best,
Aisha
Security Manager, Greenline Health
attachment: initial-compliance-questions.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Hi Aisha — thanks for sending this over. Hi Lauren / Irene — looping you in.

Summary / next steps:
- We can provide a scope inventory, an operation playbook for deletion, and a signed deletion manifest once the workflow runs.
- Short answers up front: customer data = objects (S3 for Private), DB snapshots, model KV caches tied to tenant id, and tokens/embeddings stored in our tenant-scoped object stores. Audit logs and platform telemetry are separated and retained under our monitoring SLAs (we can map what is tenant-identifiable).
- Backups: for Private EU deployments we do not enable cross-region replication by default. DR replication is configurable per-customer; if you do not opt in, snapshots remain in EU buckets managed under your VPC private endpoints.

I'll assemble a concise packet with: inventory of artifacts + locations, deletion playbook, and a sample signed manifest. Target: first packet in 48 hours; a formal attestation (engineer-signed + legal) within 7 business days.

Questions for you: does your audit require key destruction (customer-managed KMS key) or is a signed manifest + key rotation sufficient?

I'll attach the internal playbook draft and manifest template.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick clarifying items from CS side — Aisha, can you confirm the following so we scope the packet correctly:

- Is the scope limited to production tenant data in the EU (yes/no)?
- Any third-party vendor you require evidence from (backup storage providers, monitoring vendors)?
- Do you require a signed deletion certificate per tenant, or a monthly roll-up report?

Practical notes: when we run a tenant wipe in Private, our standard flow is:
  1) schedule wipe window and freeze new writes
  2) truncate tenant DB and delete logical objects
  3) rotate/destroy tenant KMS keys (if customer uses Redwood-managed keys) or provide key-rotation proof when customer manages keys
  4) run recursive object-store scrub and produce SHA256-manifest for deleted objects
  5) produce engineer-signed manifest + upload to secure drive (shared link)

We want to tailor the evidence (manifest format, certificate language) to your auditors. Any constraints?

Thanks — Lauren
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus / Lauren — that flow looks promising. A few follow-ups from our audit lead:

- We require a per-tenant deletion certificate signed by an engineer and a legal attestation for contract records.
- For backups: confirm whether any snapshots are ever copied to non-EU storage in any part of your orchestration pipeline (build pipeline, analytics backups). If anything is copied to offsite vendor storage, we need a written exclusion or vendor attestation.
- KMS: Greenline will use Customer-Managed KMS keys. We need a documented timeline for key revocation and confirmation that key destruction will render snapshots unreadable.
- Evidence format: SHA256 manifest + timestamped engineer signature acceptable. We may request chain-of-custody logs for one sample deletion as proof.

Also can you provide an estimated turnaround for the signed cert and for the legal attestation? We are pushing procurement to close this week, so speed helps.

Aisha
Security Manager, Greenline Health

Aisha — appreciate the specifics. Below is what Redwood can commit to for Greenline Health (Private / VPC, EU deployment):

1) Residency guarantees
- All customer-controlled object stores and DB snapshots for your tenant will be provisioned in EU S3-compatible buckets tied to your VPC endpoints. By default we do not enable cross-region replication for Private deployments unless explicitly configured in the tenant manifest.
- Build/CI artifacts and platform analytics are on separate accounts and do not contain tenant PII; we will provide a vendor attestation for any third-party providers used in build/backup paths.

2) Deletion and evidence workflow
- Scope: logical DB content, object-store blobs (embeddings, files), KV caches persisted to object storage, and user-provided export bundles. Platform telemetry and aggregated metrics are excluded but we will map tenant-identifiable subsets.
- Execution: schedule wipe, freeze writes, run a recursive object deletion and scrub (zero-out where supported), truncate and snapshot DB deltas, rotate or destroy Redwood-managed KMS keys. For customer-managed keys we will record key-revocation time and produce logs showing snapshot unreadability.
- Evidence: we will provide a SHA256 manifest of deleted object paths with timestamps + an engineer-signed certificate (PDF). For legal purposes we can produce a signed attestation within 7 business days of execution and a full compliance packet within 30 days.

3) Backups / snapshots
- Snapshots remain in-region unless you explicitly enable cross-region DR. We will provide an explicit configuration declaration in the tenant manifest that shows replication=false. Any third-party backup vendors will be listed and we will request their written attestation if used.

4) KMS handling
- If Greenline uses customer-managed KMS (recommended), customer retains key custody. Our platform will produce key-revocation logs and show that any snapshots encrypted with the key are unreadable after key destruction. If Redwood manages the key, we will rotate and destroy per your instruction and provide a certificate showing key destruction with a signed engineer timestamp.

Deliverables & timeline
- Packet 1 (48 hours): artifact inventory + tenant manifest showing region & replication=false + draft deletion manifest template.
- Packet 2 (within 7 business days): engineer-signed deletion certificate (PDF) and chain-of-custody logs for one sample wipe.
- Final compliance attestation (within 30 days): legal-signed attestation and audit-ready packet.

If that aligns with your audit needs we can push Packet 1 this afternoon. I will also open a HubSpot record (HS-987654) and a DocuSign request for the attestation language so legal can sign electronically.

Thanks — will follow up with the Drive link to the manifest template and sample artifacts.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
